hero.title: Sangam Economy: The Foundation of Tamilakam
hero.description: An analytical study of the agrarian, maritime, and commercial foundations of the early Tamil kingdoms.

timeline.title: The Chronological Framework
timeline.description: The era traditionally dated between 300 BCE and 300 CE, coinciding with the rise of the Chera, Chola, and Pandya dynasties.

cards.details: Earliest references in Ashokan Edicts mentioning the Cholas, Pandyas, Keralaputras, and Satiyaputras.
Pliny the Elder writes 'Naturalis Historia', detailing the drain of Roman gold to India for pepper and pearls.

mnemonics.title: Mnemonics & Tricks to Remember
mnemonics.description: Memory triggers for the Sangam landscape (Tinai system).

items.title: K-M-M-P-N
items.decryption: The 5 physiographic divisions (Tinai) of Tamilakam, critical for Prelims questions on economy and life.

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Do not confuse Sangam economy with the Vedic economy; Sangam society was primarily pastoral-agrarian with strong merchant guilds.
Remember that iron usage was already established during the Megalithic phase, which precedes the peak Sangam period.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Geography

  • Five Eco-zones (Tinai)
  • Coastal ports (Puhar, Muziris)
  • Hinterland trade routes

Key Sectors

  • Paddy Agriculture
  • Pepper/Spice Trade
  • Pearl Fisheries

Economic Structure Mindmap

  • Agrarian Base
    • Marutam (wet land) as the hub of rice production
    • Role of the Velalar (cultivator class)
  • Trade & Commerce
    • Internal Trade: Barter system, 'Umanar' (salt merchants)
    • External Trade: Yavanas (Greeks/Romans)
    • Key Exports: Pepper, Pearls, Ivory, Textiles
TinaiRegionEconomic Activity
KurinjiMountainsHunting, Honey
MullaiPastoralCattle rearing
MarutamWet LandAgriculture (Paddy)
NeithalCoastalFishing, Salt making
